title: The Regenerative Organic Standard
summary: Clip from a regenerative-farming institute leader introducing Regenerative Organic Certification as a higher bar that adds soil health, animal welfare and worker fairness to a USDA standard he says has been watered down.

assertions.quote: that's the newest high bar standard in agriculture it's the only standard of its kind that takes into account soil health
as big food companies have moved into you know organic agriculture we've actually seen unfortunately a slight watering down of that standard

verdicts.note: Hydroponic certification and the 2018 withdrawal of the animal welfare rule are cited as weakening, but other rules such as pasture and enforcement were tightened.

assertions.quote: how are the people working in those farming systems being treated uh we really don't do a good job of that

verdicts.note: The National Organic Program regulates inputs and practices, not labour conditions or wages.

assertions.quote: are they raised in a humane way um the current organic standard doesn't account for that

verdicts.note: EU organic rules require more space, outdoor range access and restricted group sizes, and a Danish report found positive welfare consequences; EU-specific and rule-level rather than outcome-level.

7 CFR 205.238-205.239 set welfare rules, among them year-round outdoor access, no continuous total confinement, bans on gestation and farrowing crates, de-beaking and induced molting, and conditions allowing freedom of movement; the regulation does not itself compare these with conventional practice or say how they are enforced.
